title: Where the Sun stops setting
hook: In June the far north gets a Sun that never sets. Where exactly does that start?

knows: that days are long in northern summer
that the Earth's axis is tilted
doesNotKnow: the latitude where the Sun stops setting on the solstice
that it is 90 degrees minus the tilt

misconception: The Sun stays up all day only at the poles, or only well past the Arctic Circle.
objective: The learner can explain that on the June solstice the Sun does not set north of 90 - 23.4 = 66.6 N, because the night side's edge stops that far short of the pole.

claims.text: On the June solstice the Sun does not set north of about 66.6 N, which is 90 degrees minus the tilt of about 23.4 degrees; the reveal places it between the highest latitude where the learner saw a sunset and the lowest where they saw none (computed by dayHours() in Demo.tsx).
claims.source: Day length from cos(H) = -tan(lat) tan(dec) with dec = 23.44 (obliquity, IAU / Astronomical Almanac, from memory): H reaches 180 degrees (24 h of day) when lat >= 90 - 23.44 = 66.56. Geometric centre of the Sun, airless spherical Earth. Computed in Demo.tsx. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: In this model, at 65.0 N the solstice day is 21 h 07 min long.
claims.source: Same formula, lat = 65: cos(H) = -tan 65 x tan 23.44 = -0.931, H = 158.6 degrees, day = 2H/15 = 21.1 h. Computed live in Demo.tsx (scratch b.mjs agrees: 21.12 h).

claims.text: The line at 66.6 N is the Arctic Circle.
claims.source: The Arctic Circle is defined as the parallel at 90 degrees minus the obliquity, about 66.56 N today (Astronomical Almanac; any atlas). From memory, not checked online.

claims.text: Because air bends sunlight and the Sun is a disc, the real midnight Sun can be seen a little south of the line.
claims.source: Standard sunrise/sunset is defined at a Sun-centre altitude of -0.833 degrees (34 arcmin refraction plus 16 arcmin semi-diameter; USNO / Astronomical Almanac). With that, the solstice midnight Sun reaches roughly 65.7 N. From memory, not checked online; the lesson gives no number for it.

claims.text: 23.4 N is the Tropic of Cancer, where the Sun is directly overhead at noon on the June solstice; it is not where the Sun stops setting. June 21 is the longest day of the year in the northern hemisphere.
claims.source: Standard geography references (Tropic of Cancer at the Sun-declination limit of about 23.44 N; June solstice about 21 June). · Fact-check pass 19 2026-10-14: VERIFIED. Tropic latitude = solar declination limit (23.44 N); on the June solstice the subsolar point is at the declination, so noon Sun is overhead there. "June 21": the solstice falls on June 20-22 depending on year and time zone; declination one day off the solstice differs by 0.0035 deg, so day length differs by seconds. Suggest "around June 21" if the builder touches the text.

claims.text: The day strip shows, hour by hour on the solstice, when the Sun is above the horizon at the town (yellow), computed from the angular distance between the town and the Sun point at 23.44 N.
claims.source: strip in Demo.tsx uses geoDistance(town, subsolar point) < 90 degrees for each hour; same model as the Daylight readout.

claims.text: In June the north pole leans 23.4 degrees toward the Sun, so the night side's edge stops 23.4 degrees short of the pole (the orange 'gap = tilt' arc on the globe, from the night edge to the pole along the midnight meridian); a place whose daily circle fits inside that gap stays in sunlight all day.
claims.source: The night side is the 90-degree circle centred on the antisolar point at 23.44 S; along its meridian it reaches 90 − 23.44 = 66.56 N, leaving 23.44 degrees to the pole. Geometry in Demo.tsx (night, gap). Reveal paragraph 2. | Added 2026-10-14 (v3) by demo-builder.

recall.question: If the Earth's axis were tilted 30 degrees instead of 23.4, where would the June midnight Sun begin?
recall.why: The night side's edge stops one tilt short of the pole, so the Sun stops setting at 90 minus the tilt: 90 - 30 = 60 N.
